logline: Two timelines - a 1990s motel owner scarred by a serial killer's stay, and a present-day pension house owner confronting a suspicious woman and her child - converge around a detective still haunted by the original case.

bollymeter.basis: 56 percent from 9 critics on Rotten Tomatoes and a 6.8 on IMDb reflect a series that divided critics sharply - performances by Kim Yoon-seok and Go Min-si drew consistent praise while the dual-timeline structure attracted both admiration and frustration.

seasons.review_body: The Frog dropped on Netflix on August 23, 2024 - originally titled 'In the Woods With No One Around' in Korean. The eight-episode mystery weaves two timelines: a 1990s motel owner shattered when a serial killer stayed at his establishment, and a present-day pension house owner who discovers a woman and child have vanished, leaving behind disturbing evidence. A detective connects both strands. Nine critics on Rotten Tomatoes awarded 56 percent, with an average of 5.7 out of 10 - the most divided critical response in this pool. Audience scores held slightly higher at 66 percent.

episode_reviews.title: Do You Know What They Call People Like Us?
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes both timelines and their tonal registers - past as slow dread, present as low-grade menace. Kim Yoon-seok's motel owner anchors the historical strand with the weight of a man who has been quietly destroyed. The structural ambiguity that would divide critics is present from the opening scene.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The serial killer checks in at the motel - and the motel owner understands, in a single exchange, that something is irrevocably wrong.

episode_reviews.title: I Think She Killed a Child
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The episode where Go Min-si's performance crosses from unsettling into genuinely frightening.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Yoo Seong-a's response to a direct accusation - the stillness, the non-reaction - confirmed Go Min-si as the show's most discussed performance.
